assistantMessage.text:
I'll explore the codebase for dashboard navigation, project title loading, and prefetch patterns. ## Route structure | Route | File | Purpose | |-------|------|---------| | `/` | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | Dashboard — lists projects | | `/projects/[slug]` | `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` | Project detail page | | Root layout | `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` | Static metadata (`title: 'Projects'`) | | Data layer | `/workspace/lib/data.ts` | Title + details fetchers | | Config | `/workspace/next.config.ts` | `cacheComponents: true` | No `loading.tsx`, `layout.tsx` under `projects/`, `generateMetadata`, or explicit prefetch/router usage anywhere in the app. --- ## 1. Dashboard page and project links **File:** `/workspace/app/page.tsx` The dashboard is a Server Component with a hardcoded project list. Each project links to `/projects/{slug}` via Next.js `Link` with default prefetch behavior (no `prefetch={false}`). ```1:21:/workspace/app/page.tsx import Link from 'next/link' const projects = [ { slug: 'acme', name: 'Acme Storefront' }, { slug: 'orbit', name: 'Orbit Analytics' }, ] export default function Dashboard() { return (

Projects

    {projects.map((project) => (
  • {project.name}
    • ))}
) } ``` **Navigation behavior:** - Client-side navigation via App Router `Link` - Default `prefetch` is enabled for static routes in the viewport — Next.js prefetches the full RSC flight payload for `/projects/[slug]`, not just the title - Dashboard already has display names (`name`) but does not pass them to the project page (no query params, no shared client state) --- ## 2. Project page — title fetch and display **File:** `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` The page wraps everything in a single `Suspense` boundary. Inside, `Project` awaits **both** `getProjectTitle` and `getProjectDetails` via `Promise.all`. ```1:33:/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx import { Suspense } from 'react' import { getProjectDetails, getProjectTitle } from '@/lib/data' export default function ProjectPage({ params }: PageProps<'/projects/[slug]'>) { return ( Loading project...}> ) } async function Project({ params, }: Pick, 'params'>) { const { slug } = await params const [title, details] = await Promise.all([ getProjectTitle(slug), getProjectDetails(slug), ]) return (

{title}

{details.description}

Recent activity

    {details.activity.map((item) => (
  • {item}
    • ))}
) } ``` **Data layer:** `/workspace/lib/data.ts` ```17:32:/workspace/lib/data.ts export async function getProjectTitle(slug: string) { 'use cache' return projects[slug]?.title ?? 'Unknown project' } export async function getProjectDetails(slug: string) { 'use cache' await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 800)) return ( projects[slug] ?? { title: 'Unknown project', description: 'This project could not be found.', activity: [], } ) } ``` **Current title behavior:** - `getProjectTitle` is effectively instant (sync lookup, `'use cache'`) - `getProjectDetails` has an artificial **800ms delay** - Because both are in one `Promise.all` inside one `Suspense` child, the fallback `"Loading project..."` shows until **both** resolve — so the title is blocked for ~800ms even though it is available immediately - No `generateMetadata` — browser tab title stays `"Projects"` from root layout - Title is only rendered after the slow fetch completes --- ## 3. Prefetch and data-fetching patterns | Pattern | Present? | Details | |---------|----------|---------| | `Link` default prefetch | Yes (implicit) | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` — no `prefetch={false}` | | `router.prefetch()` | No | Not used | | `loading.tsx` | No | — | | `generateMetadata` | No | — | | Nested `Suspense` / streaming | No | Single boundary for entire page | | `'use cache'` | Yes | Both fetchers in `/workspace/lib/data.ts` | | `cacheComponents` | Yes | `/workspace/next.config.ts` | ```1:7:/workspace/next.config.ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } export default nextConfig ``` **Effective prefetch/fetch flow today:** 1. On dashboard, `Link` prefetches the full `/projects/[slug]` RSC payload when the link is in viewport. 2. On click, if prefetch completed, navigation may feel fast — but the UI still shows `"Loading project..."` until `getProjectDetails` finishes (~800ms) because of the single `Suspense` + `Promise.all`. 3. If prefetch is disabled or incomplete, the user waits for the full server render including the 800ms delay before seeing anything. There is no title-only prefetch or partial streaming. --- ## 4. Recommendations: show title instantly without prefetching the full page ### A. Split Suspense boundaries (highest impact, minimal change) Decouple fast title from slow details so the title streams immediately: ```tsx // Conceptual structure for /workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx export default function ProjectPage({ params }: PageProps<'/projects/[slug]'>) { return (
Loading project...}> Loading details...

}>
) } ``` `ProjectTitle` only calls `getProjectTitle`; `ProjectDetails` only calls `getProjectDetails`. Title appears on first paint of the streamed chunk without waiting for details. ### B. Add `generateMetadata` for instant tab title Use `getProjectTitle(slug)` in `generateMetadata` so the document title updates as soon as metadata resolves (often before or alongside body streaming): ```tsx export async function generateMetadata({ params }: PageProps<'/projects/[slug]'>) { const { slug } = await params const title = await getProjectTitle(slug) return { title } } ``` ### C. Disable full-route prefetch if desired If the goal is to avoid prefetching the entire project page: ```tsx {project.name} ``` This stops viewport prefetch of the full RSC payload. Title instantness then depends on server streaming (A) or client-side optimistic UI (D), not prefetch. ### D. Optimistic title from dashboard (no server round-trip for title) Dashboard already has `project.name`. Options: - **Client component** that sets the `

` from `name` on click (e.g. via React context or `sessionStorage`) while details load in the background. - **URL state:** `href={`/projects/${slug}?name=${encodeURIComponent(name)}`}` and read `searchParams` for immediate display, with server fetch as source of truth for details. Useful when you want zero wait for the heading even before the server responds. ### E. Project-level layout for shared fast shell Add `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/layout.tsx` that fetches only the title in its own `Suspense`, with `page.tsx` handling details. Keeps the shell (title, nav) stable across sub-routes if you add more later. ### F. Consolidate data access `getProjectDetails` already returns `title`. Consider: - Title-only path: `getProjectTitle` (fast) - Details path: `getProjectDetails` (slow, no title needed in page if title is in a separate boundary) Avoid `Promise.all` for unrelated latency tiers. --- ## Summary | Concern | Current state | |---------|---------------| | Dashboard → project nav | `Link` to `/projects/[slug]`, default prefetch on | | Title source | `getProjectTitle(slug)` — instant lookup | | Title display delay | ~800ms — blocked by `Promise.all` with slow `getProjectDetails` | | Prefetch | Implicit full-page RSC prefetch via `Link`; no custom prefetch logic | | Best quick fix | Nested `Suspense` + `generateMetadata`; optionally `prefetch={false}` on links | The main bottleneck is architectural: one `Suspense` boundary and `Promise.all` tie the fast title to the slow details fetch. Splitting those concerns gives an instant title without relying on full-page prefetch.
